title: Love likewise: not absolute-faith act for Rome, yet included in living formed faith
source_text: LXX. Similiter quoque res se habet de Dilectione. Nam vidimus quosdam inter Reformatos negare dilectionem esse fidei actum, alios vero istud docere atque affirmare. Omnes vero Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae in ea esse sententia, quod dilectio non sit fidei actus, sed ad aliam virtutem pertineat, nempe ut jam dictum, si fidei natura absolute consideretur. Alioquin ultro fatentur fidem vivam & formatam dilectionem includere, & credere in Deum, qui est illius actus, esse Deum amare, & in Deum tendere.
pass_a_gloss: Similarly also the matter stands concerning Love. For we have seen some among the Reformed deny that love is an act of faith, others teach and affirm it. But all the Doctors of the Roman Church are of the opinion that love is not an act of faith but belongs to another virtue — namely, as already said, if the nature of faith is considered absolutely. Otherwise they freely confess that living and formed faith includes love, and that to believe in God, which is its act, is to love God and to tend into God.
pass_b_english: On dilectio some Reformed deny it is a faith-act, others affirm; all Romans say love is not an absolute-faith act but another virtue.
Yet they freely grant living formed faith includes love, and credere in Deum means loving God and tending into God.
